## Audit probe — angle-bracket survival through this write path

Not lane state. Posted to measure, precisely, which angle-bracket forms survive a body written through the GitHub MCP tools, because the seat post currently asserts a mechanism ("the GitHub body sanitizer strips angle-bracket-delimited content") that a counter-observation contradicts: dependabot's PR bodies (#4945, #4958) carry hundreds of literal HTML tags intact. If those survive and mine do not, the variable is the write path, not GitHub. This comment will be read back and the result recorded; it can be deleted afterwards.

Five forms, each on its own line, each labelled so a missing one is identifiable by its label alone:

- **A · HTML comment:** <!-- os-dev-report -->
- **B · JSX tag in prose:** <div className="x">
- **C · TS generic in prose:** Array<{ a: string }>
- **D · bare comparison in prose:** a < b and c > d
- **E · pre-escaped entity:** <div>

Fenced block, same five:

```
A <!-- os-dev-report -->
B <div className="x">
C Array<{ a: string }>
D a < b and c > d
E <div>
```

Inline code spans: A `<!-- os-dev-report -->` · B `<div className="x">` · C `Array<{ a: string }>` · D `a < b > c`

Control (must survive, proves the comment itself landed): ZZCONTROL-SENTINEL-5560.

**Audit note — round 7, cross-repo finding raised for the maintainer's attention.** Seat post body is authoritative; this comment records one item ahead of the round-close rewrite because it names a production-affecting shape in the *other* repo, outside this seat's lane.

**`objectstack-ai/objectstack#10928`**, filed by the #4765 dev while measuring the installed spec. Unassigned and unlabelled — deliberately, because it is an `objectstack` card and neither the labelling nor the grading is this seat's to do.

The shape: `UniqueScopeSchema`'s rejection message calls `'organization'` "the explicit spelling of `true`" on **both** surfaces. Measured against installed GA 17.0.0, that is false on one of them — on a *declared index*, bare `true` is the positional spelling of `'global'`, not `'organization'`. The helper readout is unambiguous:

| value | `isUniqueDeclared` | `isGlobalUnique` | `isOrganizationUnique` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `true` | true | false | false |
| `'global'` | true | true | false |
| `'organization'` | true | false | true |

Bare `true` sets neither scope flag, so no organization key part is prepended — which is precisely what makes it `'global'` on that surface.

**Why it is worth the maintainer's eye rather than the queue's.** An author refused on that key is told by the error message itself to write `'organization'`. Doing so **silently changes materialization** — the driver prepends the NULL-safe organization key part — on an index that may already exist on deployed databases. That is the unannounced reinterpretation the #8323 ruling and the #5082 sequencing exist to prevent, arriving through the error text rather than through a schema change.

Duplicate-searched before filing (two searches, objectstack repo). Nearest prior art is #8463 / PR #8512, which corrected the same field-vs-index divergence on a **different** artifact — `isOrganizationScopedUnique`'s JSDoc in driver-sql — not on the shared error map.

**Relevance to this lane, and why it changed a fix here.** The same divergence is why #5614 does *not* uniformly rewrite `unique: true`: at **field** level bare `true` is not deprecated at all ("stays valid indefinitely … no trap" per the spec's own prose), so harmonizing both occurrences would have shipped a fresh piece of false guidance on a card whose entire purpose is stopping exactly that. The dev caught this by measuring rather than by following the card, and the card is better for it.

2. **Clause ② trips on the SURFACE, not the package.** Round 17 has one card editing `packages/types` that **does** trip (`theme.zod.ts` re-exports spec zod validators by reference — the spec-mirroring face) and one editing `packages/auth` that does **not** (an internal React hook no metadata author writes against). **Two maintainer instructions recorded in §1 as policy, superseding inherited lines:** 「并发保持3」 (replaces the standing batch-5) and 「你虽然是 opus，但是可以派 fable 的卡」 — the latter is why round 17's clause-② card went out **at** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` instead of below-tier with a compensating label, which matters here because `needs:contract-review` does not exist in this repo at all (`ensure-pm-labels.sh:238` creates it for objectstack only).

**In:** `session_019ZyKZejBWZoCSj1NP35wcp`, at the maintainer's explicit direction — verbatim: 「你接手」. **Out:** `session_01EuPCi56cnGyykygi3z9w4m`, dark since its 17:57Z body write.

## The mutex readings, and the one that mattered

Recorded so the next reader can re-check rather than trust me. The three prescribed readings **all read clear**:

1. Last shift briefing in the body = **17:57Z** (~10 h, many rounds stale).
2. Newest open-round marker = the R33 dispatch line, ~17:50Z — equally stale.
3. Newest non-self `Claim:` on a `pm:dispatched` card in this lane = **none — there are zero `pm:dispatched` cards in the lane.**

⛔ **All three were clear and all three were wrong.** Fourteen cards closed in this lane between 19:44Z and 02:51Z, and five PRs merged in a single queue trip at 02:50:2x–02:50:38Z — sixteen minutes before this session began reading. A session was working the seat the whole time.

**Reading 3 is structurally blind to it.** It looks for a claim on a card labelled `pm:dispatched`, and the working session never used that label: its cards went `pm:queue` → closed. So "no `pm:dispatched` cards" read as *nobody home* when it actually meant *this session doesn't use that label*.

**What settled it was one read the protocol does not ask for:** the claim comment on the **most recently closed card** (#4919), which says *"dispatched by PM session `68ad4d1a-c111-591c-9633-f2fb64fa1803`"* at 02:09:40Z, with its dev's report at 02:41:26Z and PR #5941 merged 02:50:38Z. ✅ **Proposed amendment to the mutex read, recorded in §2: also read the newest CLOSED card in the lane, not only the `pm:dispatched` ones.** A stale seat post plus an unused status label is otherwise indistinguishable from a free seat.

This session therefore **stopped short of writing** on its first pass and put the collision to the maintainer rather than claiming cards a live session was holding. The takeover proceeds only on the explicit instruction above.

## Liveness re-verified before writing anything

- `git ls-remote --heads origin 'refs/heads/claude/*'` — **zero** `claude/issue-*` branches for any open card in this lane.
- The only open `claude/issue-*` PR in the repo is **#5948** (`claude/issue-4477-…`), another lane's.
- Last landing in this lane: 02:50:38Z. Takeover at ~04:00Z, ~70 minutes of silence.

## Five half-states repaired

Every one was `pm:queue` + assigned with its PR **already merged** and no remote branch — the shape that is invisible to candidate queries (which need `pm:queue` *and* no assignee) **and** to stale-claim reclaim (which keys off a live claim). Assignees cleared on all five; details in §3.

**#4015 got more than an assignee clear, because its label was actively lying.** It is the maintainer's Option-C decision anchor; the objectui residue landed as PR #5907 and the enforcement lands upstream (objectstack#11437 / PR #11560, relayed by the spec seat at 03:28Z). It was advertising `pm:queue` — dispatchable — when nothing on it is dispatchable here. Moved to `pm:blocked` with `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectstack#11437` written into the body so the unlock scan can reach it.

⚠️ **Two judgments left deliberately un-made, and flagged rather than silently resolved:** #5674 and #5605 both landed **stage 1 of a two-stage retirement**, with stage 2 separately carded (#5892, #5919) and currently `pm:on-hold` — whose gating condition ("stage-1 deprecation shipping") has **now fired**. Whether the stage-1 cards should close and the stage-2 cards unpark is a triage grading call, not this seat's. Assignees cleared; state otherwise untouched.

## One platform fact that reverses a standing instruction in §5

⛔ **The REST channel the predecessor's notes tell the next PM to use is dead in this session.** `GH_TOKEN` is set, but `curl https://api.github.com/...` returns **403**: `GitHub access is not enabled for this session. An org admin must connect the Claude GitHub App for this organization.` The refusal is the agent proxy's, not GitHub's.

That instruction existed because **MCP `list_issues`'s `labels` parameter is an OR, not an AND** — re-confirmed independently at takeover: `domain:ui` ∩ `pm:dispatched` returned **135** items against the lane's own **132**, and a result wider than either input is the tell. With REST unavailable the working method is to request **one** label and intersect client-side over two pages. Recorded in §5 so the next session does not spend a round rediscovering a 403.

## Four inherited items corrected by measurement, not inherited

1. **⛔ The body's #5522 warning is half-wrong, and the wrong half is the actionable one.** It says the pre-existing branch `claude/issue-5522-sentry-disableable-telemetry` "carries real work — declare continue-or-replace". Those two commits (`e94b85847`, `f751c0288`) **are PR #5559, which merged 2026-08-21**. Verified on `origin/main`: `.env.production` carries no DSN (and now carries a long warning comment), `resolveSentryGate` exists, `sendDefaultPii` is opt-in, the ratchet test is in place. The branch is **spent, not WIP** — the next dev replaces, it does not continue.
2. **#5522's real remaining scope is the consumer half, and its blocker is gone.** objectstack#10805 closed 2026-08-23T16:57Z via **merged PR objectstack#11382** ("serve a fail-closed SPA telemetry permission on `/api/v1/runtime/config`"). 4. **#2477's item 2 appears already landed** — `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/__tests__/studioChatDockPersistence.test.tsx` exists on `main`. ## ⛔ #5980 could NOT be dispatched, and the previous marker was wrong to promise it

The R35 close-out named #5980 "front of R36". **It carries no labels at all** — no `domain:*`, no pm-state. Under the single-producer rule, `domain:*` comes only from the triage seat and **未打标签的 issue 任何人不得认领**. Claiming it would have been this seat producing a routing label.

Reported to triage instead; it goes out the round after it is graded. ⚠️ Recording the near-miss because the pull was real: the card is a doc teaching a shape #5981 **just made refused**, so it feels urgent — and that is exactly when a seat is most likely to reach across the single-producer line.

## Two cards carry embedded judgements, and the briefs say which kind

**#5956/#5957** both name a decision (what a `won` terminus should announce; whether the lost group should be announced at all). Briefed as **accessibility/copy judgements inside the fence — make them and justify them, ⛔ do not escalate a wording choice** — with a stop-and-report if either turns out to change what a stage *means* rather than what it *says*.

**#5930** self-describes as a contract question with three options. Two are already settled by evidence on the tree (⛔ `LazyIcon` ruled out by #5622/#5633 — it degrades an unknown name to the `Database` glyph, trading a no-icon failure for a wrong-icon one; ⛔ retiring the key is the manual floor). So it went out as a **ruling with a falsifiable premise attached**: route is `resolveIcon`, premise is that `resolveIcon` is reachable from `renderers/overlay/` without a layering inversion, and ⛔ if the premise fails the dev reports the fork rather than silently switching options.

## 🎉 The decision inbox is EMPTY — and that is new state this seat did not produce

## ⛔ `total_count` IS NOT A CONSTANT — do not judge a gate read by "22"

I did not wave it away, and the reason it is safe is worth writing down because the two cases look identical in a count and are completely different in meaning:

- **A job-level `if:` produces a check run with `conclusion: skipped`.** It is present, it counts, and its absence would be a real anomaly.
- **A workflow-level `paths:` filter produces NO check run at all.** The workflow never triggers, so nothing appears — and the count drops.

Measured, not assumed: `Bundle Analysis` lives in `.github/workflows/performance-budget.yml`, which carries a **workflow-level `paths:`** filter (lines 6 and 12). #6028's diff is `examples/schema-catalog/**` + `content/docs/plugins/**` + a changeset — no package source — so the workflow legitimately did not fire. 21 of 21 completed, 18 `success` + 3 `skipped`, **zero failures**, `Vercel` green. Enqueued.

**Corrected judge, replacing the count-based one:**

> ✅ **Every check run PRESENT is `completed` with a non-failing conclusion, AND every expected check that is ABSENT is explained by a workflow-level `paths:` filter that the diff genuinely does not match.**
> ⛔ Never "the count is 22". ⛔ `in_progress` is still not a verdict, and `mergeable_state: unknown` is still not `clean`.

⚠️ The failure this protects against is the inverse of the one §5 was written for: a count-based judge would have **held a clean PR** here, and — worse — would happily pass a PR where a check was absent because a workflow was **broken or deleted**, since that also lowers the count. The discriminator is the *reason* for the absence, and it costs one `grep` of `.github/workflows/`.

## ⭐ Lane fact learned the expensive way — file-surface disjointness does NOT imply bundle-budget disjointness

`domain:ui` seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`, R1. Audit note; folds into §4 of the body at the next round-boundary refresh.

### What happened

PR **#7391** (#7210 + #7225) went **red on Bundle Analysis — per-chunk ceiling**, at head `c5a46298c`. The gate's own breakdown: aggregate ✅, per-chunk ❌, sensitivity ✅, **freshness ✅** — freshness passing is what rules out a stale-baseline artefact, so the overage is real.

Its dev had already measured the risk and called it: it attributed exactly 1,075 gzipped bytes to its branch against a control build of plain `origin/main`, **declined to raise the ceiling** (correctly — a gate threshold is a `门禁削弱` item on the maintainer's floor), paid for the bytes by tightening the footnote copy to the ruling's own wording, landed at 511.6 KB against a 511.7 KB ceiling, and wrote the warning into its own commit message: *"0.2 KB is not comfort … CI weighs the MERGE ref, so another lane landing framework bytes first can turn this red with no further change here."*

Three commits landed on `main` inside that window. **Two of them were this seat's**: `7776fc268` (#7349, `packages/core`) and `b65251465` (#7182, `packages/types` + `packages/components`) — and `types (ui-action.js)` grew **3.40 KB → 8.11 KB** across it.

### The rule this exposes

Batch independence in this loop is defined on **file surfaces**: "no two cards in a batch may touch the same package / registry / barrel / spec schema." #7349, #7182 and #7210+#7225 satisfied that completely — `packages/core`, `packages/types`+`components`+`plugin-detail`, and the four non-grid plugin views. Disjoint by construction, and correctly dispatched.

⇒ **They still collided.** The console's per-chunk eager-closure budget is a **shared serial resource across the whole lane**, exactly like the merge queue — and unlike the merge queue, nothing in the dispatch protocol surfaces it. Three PRs can be file-disjoint, individually green, and still push one chunk over between them, with the failure landing on whichever one merges **last** rather than on whichever one spent the bytes.

### What this seat will do differently, and hands to its successor

- ⚠️ **Treat "adds bytes to an eagerly-loaded chunk" as a serial constraint of its own**, alongside the hot-file queue. Cards that add i18n keys, new exports on `@object-ui/react` / `@object-ui/types`, or renderer copy are the population; the seat post's serial-queue table is the natural home for it.
- **Name it in the claim's `Serial constraints cleared` line** when a card is in that population, rather than only listing file-surface siblings.
- ⚠️ **Landing order matters and is the PM's to sequence.** When one in-flight card is measuring against a tight per-chunk ceiling, landing a sibling that adds bytes to the same chunk first is a choice, not a neutral act — and the cost falls on the card that did the measuring.
- The existing lane fact ("per-chunk eager-closure ceilings have little headroom — one key across ten packs fits, forty do not") was **necessary but not sufficient**: it warns a dev about its own bytes, and says nothing about the bytes arriving from its siblings while it works.

⛔ Recorded as this seat's miss, not the lane's. The dev flagged the exposure in advance and I read the warning without drawing the sequencing conclusion from it.

## Platform fact, learned by getting it wrong: on a queue-protected branch, `auto_merge: none` does NOT mean "not enqueued"

`domain:ui` seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. Later than the body's last edit, so it is in the read path. Recording because the wrong inference here is cheap to make and expensive to act on.

### What happened landing PR #7409

1. All 30 checks resolved green ⇒ flipped the PR out of draft, called `enable_pr_auto_merge` (SQUASH).
2. The tool replied **"Auto-merge enabled … (method: , enabled at )"** — an empty method and an empty timestamp.
3. `git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-7409-*'` returned **nothing**, and so did the whole-queue pattern. The control (`refs/heads/main`) fired, so the probe was working.
4. The PR's own JSON read **`auto_merge: none`**, with `mergeable: true`, `mergeable_state: clean`.

⇒ I concluded the call had been a **no-op** — the tool's contract says it "fails gracefully … if the PR is already mergeable (clean status)", and the PR had gone `clean` the moment the last shard turned green. That reading was **wrong**.

5. Calling `merge_pull_request` returned **`405 Pull Request is in the merge queue`**, and a re-run of the same `ls-remote` then showed `refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-7409-7c7729859b…`.

### The corrected facts

- ⭐ **On a branch protected by a merge queue, enabling auto-merge on a `clean` PR enqueues it immediately** — it does not sit in an auto-merge pending state. `auto_merge` therefore stays **`null`**, because the PR is *queued*, not *waiting to auto-merge*. ⛔ `auto_merge: none` is NOT evidence against enqueue on such a branch.
- ⭐ **The `gh-readonly-queue` ref appears seconds AFTER the enqueue**, when GitHub creates the test branch. A single `ls-remote` fired immediately after enqueuing is a **false negative** — and a control that fires does not save you, because the control proves the probe works, not that the ref has been created yet. ⇒ **This is a race, not a reading.** Re-probe before concluding.
- The empty `method:` / `enabled at` echo is still just cosmetic noise, as previously recorded. ⛔ It is not a signal of a no-op — I misread it as one.
- `405 Pull Request is in the merge queue` is a **success signal**, not a failure: it is the branch protection refusing a direct merge because the queue owns the merge. It is also the cheapest positive confirmation available when the ref has not appeared yet.

### The general lesson, which is the reusable half

This is the same failure mode this seat has been catching in others all shift, arriving from a new direction: **a zero taken at the wrong moment**. The lane's rule has been "a zero is only a reading if a control fires" — that rule is necessary and, here, **not sufficient**. The control fired and the zero was still false, because the thing being probed had not been created yet.

⇒ **Amended rule: for state that a remote system creates asynchronously, a control proves the probe, and only a re-probe after the state settles proves the absence.** For enqueue specifically, confirm by either the `gh-readonly-queue` ref OR a `405 … in the merge queue`, and re-probe once before reporting "not enqueued".

### Current state of #7409

Enqueued and **first in the queue** — the ref suffix is `7c7729859b…`, which is `main`'s own head, and per the existing lane fact the suffix names the entry ahead of it (or `main` when first). One entry in the queue, nothing ahead. #7212 stays `pm:dispatched` until it merges, then the landing gets verified BY CONTENT on `origin/main` with a live control, as with the other four this shift.
